record.:question/problem:
Find the particular solution to the differential equation $y'=- 6 x- 2 e^{- 2 x}$ that satisfies the condition $y(0)=-4.$

$y=\,${{field-1}}
record.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative is already isolated, so we have

$$
y'=- 6 x- 2 e^{- 2 x}.
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x,$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int y'\,\text{d}x & =\int (- 6 x- 2 e^{- 2 x})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\int (- 6 x)\,\text{d}x + \int (- 2 e^{- 2 x})\,\text{d}x \\ & =(-6)(\frac{x^{2}}{2}) + (-2)(- \frac{e^{- 2 x}}{2})+C \\ & =- 3 x^{2}+e^{- 2 x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

So our general solution is $y=- 3 x^{2}+e^{- 2 x}+C.$ To find a particular solution, we substitute the condition $y(0)=-4$ into our solution and obtain a value for $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =(- 3 (0)^{2}) + (e^{- 2 (0)})+C \\ -4 & =(0) + (1)+C \\ C & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
y=- 3 x^{2} - 5 + e^{- 2 x}.
$$

$$

So our general solution is $g(x)=\frac{4 x^{3}}{3}- \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}+2 \sin{(x )}+C.$ To find a particular solution, we substitute the condition $g(0)=-2$ into our solution and obtain a value for $C,$ as follows:

$$
